FEB 2 2025 HON. EDZEL L. LONZANIDA. MD Mayor. Municipality of San Antonio, Province of Zambales This pertains to your Letter dated 18 September 2024, with subject: dQuery on the secunng application of foreign travel authority of local official" Per your representation, the Liga ng mga Barangay President Rolando a. Borja took a vacation leave from August 1 to October I, 2024 and traveled to the United States without previously getting approval from the Mayor's Office. You now pose the questions as to whether Borja violated DILG MC No. 2022-174 and the proper administraåve sanctions. First, the requirement for foreign travel authority under DILG MC No. 2022-174 is anchored on Section 6 of OP Memorandum Circular No. 35, s. 2017 provides that "no govemment official or employee shall be allowed to depart for any travel abroad, even if such travel is for purely personal or private purpose without cost to the government, unless such official or employee has duly accomplished the requisite leave forms and has obtained the appropriate travel authorization from his or her agency." Moreover, DILG MC No. 2022-174 provides that the approving authority for foreign travels of sangguniang bayan members is vested with the Mayor for unofficial trips when the period of travel is less than three (3) months and when there is no emergency or crisis. Considering that LNB President Borja proceeded with his foreign travel lasting for about two months without prior authority from the Mayor, he is deemed to have violated OP Memorandum Circular No. 35, s. 2017. Second, as regards administrative sanctions Sec. 7 of OP Memorandum Circular No. 35, s. 2017 provides that "administrative cases for misconduct, insubordination or other related offenses under the Civil Service Commission Revised Rules on Administrative Cases in the Civil Service and/or other relevant laws, rules and regulations snail be filed against govemment personnel traveling abroad without the requisite authority. The filing of said cases shall be without prejudice to other liabilities and personnel actions allowed under existing laws, rules and regulations. " Finally, this opinion is based solely on the facts and representations narrated from the letter and our appreciation of the same. Further, this opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No. (02) 8876 3454

Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: ATTY. ROMEO P. BENITEZ Undersecretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs Page20f2
